items.title: What Dunning and Kruger actually showed
items.claim: Dunning and Kruger (1999) reported a finding that became internet shorthand. Their actual graph showed something subtler. Which is closest?

options.text: The least competent rated themselves below average
Most people overestimated their performance; the lowest performers overestimated the most
The most competent thought they were the worst

items.reveal_title: Most people overestimated; the least competent overestimated most
items.reveal:
In the original study, participants in the bottom quartile of test performance rated themselves around the 62nd percentile.

Statisticians (Nuhfer et al., 2017) have argued part of the effect is regression to the mean rather than pure metacognitive failure.
items.why: Popular versions of findings often lose the nuance that makes them scientifically interesting.

items.title: Cognitive load theory shapes instructional design
items.claim: John Sweller's cognitive load theory (1988 onwards) distinguishes three types of load. Which design principle follows directly?

options.text: Always make instructions as long as possible

Minimise extraneous load (poor design) and manage intrinsic load (task complexity) so working memory can devote capacity to germane load (schema formation) — worked examples for novices, problem-solving for experts (expertise reversal effect)

items.reveal_title: Working memory is the bottleneck for learning
items.reveal:
Sweller's theory builds on Miller's 7+/-2 and Baddeley's working memory. Educational applications include worked-example effect (better than problem-solving for novices), modality effect (combining visual + auditory exceeds visual alone), redundancy effect (repeating information harms learning).

David Geary distinguishes 'biologically primary' knowledge (language, faces) that we acquire effortlessly from 'biologically secondary' (reading, algebra) that requires designed instruction. The theory has reshaped UK curriculum guidance (EEF 2018, Ofsted 2019).
items.why: Teaching that ignores working memory limits — long instructions, complex diagrams, novice problem-solving — is measurably less effective. CLT puts a constraint into instructional design.

items.title: What split-brain patients reveal
items.claim: Roger Sperry's split-brain research (Nobel Prize 1981) studied patients whose corpus callosum had been severed to treat what condition?
items.reveal_title: The surgery was a last-resort epilepsy treatment
items.reveal:
Commissurotomy was performed to prevent seizures from spreading between hemispheres. Sperry and Gazzaniga then used these patients to study hemispheric specialisation in the 1960s and 70s.

The research showed each hemisphere could process information independently when communication was cut.
items.why: Some of the most important findings about the brain came from rare clinical populations.
